8c266b9ba995444a9ed5a801dbd1f0b71cc8021c.summary: CrowdStrike reports a significant rise in eCrime actors using ransomware against VMware ESXi hypervisors since its February 2021 post on hypervisor jackpotting. It describes ESXi-targeting campaigns by several SPIDER-named actors, using tools including Babuk Locker, DeathKitty, Pysa, REvix and Ragnar Locker, with tradecraft such as SSH access and terminating VMs before encryption. It recommends avoiding direct host access, restricting vCenter exposure, backing up datastores daily, and not shutting down hosts during encryption.

8c07515bff49058298298366cbfa89478d71b47f.summary: Zscaler ThreatLabz blog post by Javier Vicente Vallejo, published 2024-01-31, tracing about 15 years of Qakbot malware development. It describes changes to the command-and-control protocol, encryption moving from RC4 to AES, a time-based domain generation fallback added in version 2.0.1, compromised FTP servers used for data exfiltration before that was changed, compromised systems used as relays, and RSA signatures added in version 3.0.0.443.
